description.narrative: Disaster preparedness and response coordination mechanism (the Mechanism) strengthened through effective DRCU Secretariat support. The main objective of the project is to support the coordination activities of the Disaster Response Coordination Unit (DRCU) Secretariat in further strengthening cooperation and coordination for disaster preparedness and response between the donors, local and international NGOs, including women’s groups, UN organizations and the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic. Output 3: Joint strategic response capacity upgraded based on prioritized needs Target1: One updated harmonized assessment package in place Target2: 30 REACT members and DRCU partners who practiced harmonized assessment
Output 4: Response capacities of national, international and regional actors are well coordinated and interoperable Target1: One IACPs updated based on ERP approach with the support of DRCU Secretariat Target2: 90% of Minimum Preparedness Actions (MPAs) are in place Target3: 40 Government, national and international partners involved in discussion or testing of IHA draft law and supporting documents

During 2020, all the targeted indicators within all outputs are reached.
During the reporting period, DRCU regular/planned meetings were conducted on 21 January, 10 March, 2 July and 17 November 2020. The main objective of the meetings was to discuss and decide on emerging humanitarian issues to improve overall response preparedness. The meetings covered various subjects, including quarterly risk analysis and monitoring, DRCU workplan, MoES and Government plans on emergency response, analysis of the activities within the framework of DRCU, planning for COVID-19, preparedness for inter-agency response to COVID-19 and contingency planning for severe localized violence including inter-communal clashes.
Output 2: Humanitarian decision-making improved through strengthened common situational awareness. Since the beginning of the pandemic, DRCU Secretariat and DRCU Sector Leads issued daily statistics, weekly updates and 3W updates to DRCU members. All the documents are uploaded to https://www.humanitarianresponse.info/ru/operations/kyrgyzstan/documents. During reporting period DRCU Secretariat managed the DRCU website in the global platform www.humanitarianresponse.info. The platform includes general information about DRCU and its assessment data, list of contacts, maps and info graphics. DRCU Secretariat regularly enters updated information on events conducted and documents issued. The link to the DRCU website is available on https://www.humanitarianresponse.info/en/operations/kyrgyzstan. DRCU Secretariat supported development, collection and processing data for Kyrgyzstan CODs. Common operational datasets (CODs) are authoritative reference datasets needed to support operations and decision-making for all actors in a humanitarian response. CODs are made available on the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX): https://data.humdata.org/group/kgz DRCU Secretariat developed description of business processes, supported development and testing of two modules on registration of needs in case of emergency and registration of humanitarian assistance. Online platform was financially supported by WFP and implemented by Disaster Management Crisis Center of MoES.
Output 3: Joint strategic response capacity upgraded based on prioritized needs Starting from October 2020, DRCU Secretariat organized series of online trainings for colleagues on international architecture, information management, needs assessments and mapping for AIMWG members and information management focal points from sectors. The trainings were conducted by Ms. Galiya Ibragimova, Information Management Officer, UN OCHA.
Output 4: Response capacities of national, international and regional actors are well coordinated and interoperable DRCU Secretariat supported the development and update of the Inter-Agency Contingency Plan guided by the Emergency Response Preparedness approach. DRCU Secretariat supported the coordination and implementation of preparedness for situations of violence, including a protocol of interaction with military structures and access to affected regions. On 5 March 2020, DRCU Secretariat conducted meeting on “Minimum standards for the provision of humanitarian assistance in emergency situations”. The main objective of the meeting was to provide brief overview of international humanitarian minimum standards to government partners and to discuss it by thematic sectors of respected governmental bodies. As a result zero draft of minimum standards was drafted. Technical legal expert support needed to finalize the document. DRCU supported the development of the Kyrgyzstan International Disaster Relief Law and its implementation. The law was adopted by Parliament and ratified by President on 22 June 2017. The International Disaster Relief law will ensure the coordination and provision of timely management of international assistance. As a result of inter-departmental working group and DRCU work on international disaster relief law implementation plan was developed. Implementation plan was approved by the Government Apparatus in May 2018. DRCU Secretariat is providing support to all focal points to ensure coordinated implementation of the Law.
